title: Sheafification of an explicit finite free resolution on an affine chart
statement: Let X be a scheme, U an open, and e : U.toScheme ≅ Spec A [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let M be an A-module, and let an explicit augmented exact resolution of M by finite free A-modules be given by ranks n, augmentation ε and maps d, with surjectivity and kernel-range equalities. Then there is a bounded-above cochain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] of finite free sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the over-site of U and a quasi-isomorphism to the degree-zero complex of the transported tilde of M [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The construction places the j-th free term in degree -j, applies tilde, and transports along e and the open-subscheme/over-site equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 26.5.4, Tag 01HV, functoriality and exactness of tilde; Modules Lemma 17.3.1, Tag 01AG; Algebra Lemma 10.71.1, Tag 00LP supplies the algebraic resolution used by the parent

proof.text: Define K using ChainComplex.of on the finite function modules with differentials d. The supplied kernel-range identities imply square-zero and augmentation compatibility. The degree-zero quasi-isomorphism criterion is augmented exactness plus surjectivity of ε; at each positive chain degree it is exactly hd. Package K and its augmentation as a projective resolution, since each finite function module is free.

Prove that tilde preserves kernels: the kernel of a map between tilde modules is quasi-coherent, so its tilde-global-sections counit is an isomorphism. Lift its kernel fork using full faithfulness of tilde, and reflect the limiting property. Tilde is an additive left adjoint, hence also preserves colimits. Therefore it preserves homology and quasi-isomorphisms.

Extend the projective resolution to integer cochain degrees by n ↦ -n. Apply tilde, restriction along e, and the inverse over-site equivalence termwise. These exact functors preserve the augmentation quasi-isomorphism. Compose with the canonical single-complex comparison. The bound is zero. In degree -j use the standard finite-function basis, reindex by ULift, tildeFinsupp, and mapFreeIso for both transports. In positive degrees identify the transported zero object with the free sheaf on ULift (Fin 0).

proof_origin.place: Tags 01HV and 01IC: exactness of associated sheaves and quasi-coherent kernels. The kernel-fork argument uses full faithfulness and the tilde/global-sections counit; formalized by J4 with Mathlib projective-resolution extension and homology-preserving functors.
